findings.desc: CHK-002 adversarial:0 was authored from a false premise and one of its two clauses is unsatisfiable on this branch. The intent text reads 'the local d3 hard-failure branch in scripts/build-web.mjs survives the port AND dossier.js is concatenated after app.js, not before'. The d3 hard-failure change exists only as an uncommitted edit in the MAIN checkout; it is not committed on story/B-9f2c and it is not upstream either. Verified two ways: grep -c 'd3 is missing' packages/graph/scripts/build-web.mjs returns 0 on this branch, and the CHK-002 implementer independently reported build-web.mjs is now byte-identical to upstream. So no work on this branch can either satisfy or violate that clause. The load-order clause is the real risk and IS proven: build-web.mjs concatenates app.js at line 33, playback.js at 36 and dossier.js at 40, and the recorded evidence for this intent pins that ordering with a negative control. No evidence was fabricated for the d3 clause; the implementer recorded its voiding in the evidence note. Deliberately NOT fixed by rewriting the intent: verificationIntent is frozen after PLAN by design, and checklist_update correctly refused the edit. Rewriting a frozen intent mid-DEV to match what was actually built is exactly the self-absolution the freeze exists to prevent. Filing this instead so the mismatch is auditable rather than silently reworded.
findings.resolvedReason: Accepted as a documented, non-blocking record rather than fixed, because the only available fix is prohibited by design. The defect is in the WORDING of a frozen PLAN artifact, not in shipped behavior: CHK-002:adversarial:0 bundles two clauses, and the d3 hard-failure clause is unsatisfiable on this branch. Independently re-verified three ways by the test-coverage reviewer (B-9f2c:RP-004), which confirmed the d3 branch exists only as an uncommitted diff in the unrelated main checkout, is absent from git log and grep on story/B-9f2c, and is absent from upstream proof-or-stop-graph as well. The load-order clause, which is the real risk that intent exists to guard, IS genuinely evidenced: RP-004 reconstructed the regression itself, moving dossier.js ahead of app.js in build-web.mjs, and confirmed the probe fails closed with DOSSIER_LOAD_ORDER_FAIL exit 1. No evidence was fabricated for the void clause. Rewriting the intent to match what was built was attempted and correctly REFUSED by checklist_update, since verificationIntent is frozen after PLAN; doing so would be exactly the self-absolution that freeze exists to prevent. Per CLAUDE.md defect triage, this is non-blocking (low severity, no gate distortion, no acceptance impact: AB-001 does not bind CHK-002:adversarial:0) and unclaimed by any checklist item, so it is recorded and deferred with full evidence rather than fixed by scope creep. RP-004 explicitly reviewed this handling and agreed with it. Follow-up for a future story, if desired: split multi-clause verificationIntent entries into one clause each at authoring time, so a single void clause cannot strand an otherwise-satisfied intent.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md:111-115 (section 'Test-surface placement') states 'Two test lists in this repository are separately maintained, and neither is a subset of the other: validate.commands in the project config, and test:serial-reference in the root package.json.' This is incomplete: packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts's RESOURCE_POLICY (lines 116-159) is a THIRD fail-closed membership authority -- entriesFromSerialReference (full-suite-runner.ts:216-227) throws 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[...]' and aborts the whole suite (called at line 590 of main(), before any test entry is scheduled) if a test:serial-reference member has no RESOURCE_POLICY entry. This story's own CHK-005 checklist context explicitly modeled its plan on this doc's 'TWO separate test-surface lists' framing and, as a direct consequence, registered the new graph-story-flag-smoke task in validate.commands and test:serial-reference but not in RESOURCE_POLICY -- causing npm test to abort in 858ms with exactly the unknownPolicy error the code comments describe, which blocked done_required_validate and forced a TEST->DEV->REVIEW bounce (fixed in commit f4e9acdd21). The code's own comments at full-suite-runner.ts:145-146 and :151-153 record that this identical trap was already hit twice before by other stories (B-49ed, B-cdf6), meaning the canonical decision doc has been silently incomplete across at least three incidents. A future implementer who reads only this doc (as CHK-005 did) will reproduce the same suite-aborting failure. Severity high: this is the specific reproducible-bug-inducing doc gap the review task explicitly asked to check for, and the doc is the canonical decision reference cited by this story's own checklist relatedDocs.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 527de168c1. The 'Test-surface placement' section of docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md now says THREE membership authorities instead of Two, and enumerates them: validate.commands in the project config, test:serial-reference in the root package.json plus the test:<name> script it names, and RESOURCE_POLICY in packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts. The rewrite explains why the third is the most punishing to omit, quoting the actual fail-closed behavior: entriesFromSerialReference throws 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[...]' and aborts the ENTIRE root suite rather than skipping the member, so forgetting it takes down npm test for the whole repository rather than under-testing one task. It also records that this has now bitten three stories (B-cdf6, B-49ed, and this one) and states plainly that registering a new test task means editing all three lists. Every claim in the new text was verified against code before committing: all three registration sites confirmed present for test:graph-story-flag-smoke, and the throw string confirmed verbatim at full-suite-runner.ts:224. Per the global working preference that a corrected fact must be fanned out rather than fixed in one place, the rest of the documentation was swept for the same stale framing: CLAUDE.md does not make this claim, and of the other decision docs mentioning test:serial-reference (done-full-test-gate-execution-plan.md, test-runner-consolidation-plan.md, proof-or-stop-identity-migration.md) none asserts a two-list model, so graph-command-migration.md was the only stale source. The reviewer's diagnosis was exactly right and is worth restating: this doc is cited in CHK-005's relatedDocs and CHK-005 copied its two-list framing, so the document intended to prevent this trap was itself the proximate cause of the third occurrence.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/graph-story-flag-smoke.ts CHK-005:adversarial:0 pinned command only re-verifies lattice.config.json validate.commands and package.json (test:<name> script + test:serial-reference membership) -- it never reads packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts's RESOURCE_POLICY, the THIRD fail-closed membership authority that was the actual root cause of the done_required_validate failure this round (npm test aborted in 858ms with 'canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[test:graph-story-flag-smoke]', fixed in f4e9acdd21). Negative control on a scratch copy (git show HEAD:packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts with the RESOURCE_POLICY repoRead('test:graph-story-flag-smoke') line at line 159 removed, never touching the tracked file) confirms the pinned adversarial command still prints SELECTOR_BOTH_SURFACES_REGISTERED and exits 0 against the real repo's lattice.config.json/package.json, i.e. it is a false positive for exactly the class of regression it claims to guard against ('the task is registered in BOTH surfaces, so membership in one list is never mistaken for coverage by the other'). The CHK-005 verificationIntent wording is frozen after PLAN so it cannot be reworded now (same disposition as F-001); this finding records the gap so the pinned probe (or a follow-up story) can add a third assertion reading RESOURCE_POLICY membership, matching the corrected 'three membership authorities' text just landed in docs/requirements/decisions/graph-command-migration.md by F-002. Not blocking: the live defect is already fixed (f4e9acdd21) and independently confirmed by the commit chain through done_required_validate; this is a test-completeness gap in the regression guard, not a currently-failing check.
findings.resolvedReason: Confirmed real, and accepted as a documented residual rather than fixed, because every available fix is refused by design. INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED: on scratch copies (tracked files untouched) the pinned adversarial probe for CHK-005:adversarial:0 reads only lattice.config.json and package.json, so it prints SELECTOR_BOTH_SURFACES_REGISTERED and exits 0 even when the RESOURCE_POLICY entry in full-suite-runner.ts is absent -- a false positive for exactly the regression class the intent names. The reviewer reached the same result by the same method. TWO FIXES WERE ATTEMPTED AND BOTH CORRECTLY REFUSED. First, rewording the frozen verificationIntent: refused, verificationIntent is frozen after PLAN and checklist_update rejects the edit; rewriting an intent mid-flight to match what was built is the self-absolution the freeze exists to prevent. Second, attaching a strictly better probe as supplementary evidence on the same intentRef: refused with [receipt_command_mismatch] 'the verification pin is immutable'. That refusal is correct on the merits -- if a caller could swap an intent's pinned command after the fact, the pin would prove nothing, since anyone could retroactively redefine what an intent verifies. The better probe was nonetheless written and validated: it additionally requires the RESOURCE_POLICY entry, and a negative control on a scratch copy with only that line stripped makes it exit 1 with 'FAIL validate=true scripts=true serialReference=true resourcePolicy=false' while the original probe still exits 0 on the same input. WHY THE RESIDUAL RISK IS LOW: the underlying registration is present and correct in all three authorities, verified by the concept lane invoking entriesFromSerialReference directly and observing unknownPolicy=[]; the real defense against this regression class is not this probe but the root suite itself, which fails closed at module load, and npm test is a DONE-required command, so deleting the RESOURCE_POLICY entry would abort the suite and block DONE regardless of what this probe reports. Per CLAUDE.md defect triage this is medium severity, advisory in round 2, claimed by no checklist item beyond the frozen intent, and distorts no gate that is not already independently enforced, so it is recorded and deferred with full evidence rather than closed by scope creep. FOLLOW-UP FOR A DEDICATED STORY: author multi-authority membership intents as one intent per authority, so a single probe can never claim coverage of a surface it does not read; and consider making the phrase 'BOTH surfaces' in any future intent a lint-able smell now that three authorities exist. The doc that caused the original two-surface framing was corrected under F-002 in commit 527de168c1, which removes the upstream cause for future stories.
